data.narrative:
HIMERA, a seed-stage defense and security company founded by Misha Rudominsky and Oleksiy Oliynyk, has raised $2.5M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 10 comparable companies—2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private—operating in the same sector at seed and Series A stages. Key private comparables include UFORCE, Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, and Saronic.

Two triangulation methods prove applicable. The stage-progression approach uses HIMERA's $2M raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for seed-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $6M. The peer-median method anchors to the median valuation of four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage peers at $700M, with a range spanning $125M (NODA AI) to $4.0B (Stark Defence).

The triangulated analysis produces a range from $5M (low) to $805M (high), with a median of $353M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty inherent in seed-stage valuation: the peer set exhibits substantial heterogeneity in stage progression and market positioning. The stage-progression method suggests conservative near-term valuation, while peer-median anchoring to comparables like the $1.0B seed-stage UFORCE reflects higher multiples in the defense technology market. Primary valuation risk centers on the characterization of comparable peers and HIMERA's ability to achieve comparable capital efficiency and growth trajectories within an early-stage, venture-backed cohort.
